title: Mind Map Schema
description: Schema for the Mind Map Editor's YAML format (mindmap-editor.html), which is designed to map onto Freeplane. mindmap-format.md describes the format in full. Two rules can't be checked by this schema: every connector's 'to' must be the path of a node in the same map, and keys must be unique among siblings (YAML parsers reject duplicate keys). The editor writes files that match this schema; when opening, it is more lenient, ignoring unknown fields and accepting other key characters.

title.description: The text shown on the node. May contain line breaks. Must be a string: quote values YAML would read as numbers, booleans, dates or null

icons.description: Icons shown before the title, in order, by Freeplane's built-in icon names (such as 'idea', 'yes' or 'full-1')

note.description: A note attached to the node, in Markdown (GitHub-flavoured). LaTeX maths goes between $...$ within a line or $$...$$ on its own; \$ is a literal dollar sign. Write notes containing backslashes as YAML block scalars (|), since double-quoted YAML treats \f, \n and others as escapes

link.description: An absolute web address (URL) attached to the node, such as https://example.org

connectors.description: Arrows from this node to other nodes

to.description: Path of the target node: 'root', then each child key in turn, separated by '/'

label.description: Optional text shown on the connector

children.description: Child nodes of this node, in display order. Each key names the child among its siblings and forms part of connector paths. The editor makes keys from titles: lower case, each run of other characters replaced by '_', trimmed, cut to 40 characters, 'node' if empty, with _2, _3 ... added to repeats

node.description: A node: a title, with optional icons, note, link, connectors and child nodes

root.description: The central topic. On opening, the first half of its children (rounded up) go to the right of the map and the rest to the left
